annotation.kind: source selection, tier label, and finite data-perturbation form of Lemma 2.2

assumptions: Each data perturbation is bounded componentwise by epsilon times the magnitude of the corresponding datum.
The unperturbed interpolation value is nonzero.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P13 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P13 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p13_t2_data_perturbation_bound {n : Nat} (ell f deltaF : Fin n -> Real) (epsilon : Real) ... : abs (p13InterpolationValue ell (f+deltaF) - p13InterpolationValue ell f) / abs (p13InterpolationValue ell f) <= epsilon * p13Condition ell f
formal_statement.plain_language: A componentwise relative perturbation of the interpolation data changes the fixed-point interpolation value by at most epsilon times Higham's condition number in relative terms.

informal_proof: Multiply each data perturbation bound by the magnitude of its Lagrange coefficient, invoke the generic finite-sum componentwise perturbation theorem, and identify its condition number with equation (2.2).
informal_statement: The componentwise perturbation inequality in Lemma 2.2.

paper_source.local_path: paper_bencmark/reference_papers/P13_The numerical stability of barycentric Lagrange interpolation.pdf

paper_version: published journal version; IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis 24(4), October 2004, printed pages 547-556

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The mounted declaration handles generic summands. The L proof must translate perturbations of f_i through the paper-specific Lagrange coefficients ell_i before applying it.

tier_rationale: The L proof combines the mounted generic summation perturbation theorem with a new translation from perturbations of the interpolation data to perturbations of the weighted Lagrange summands.
